title: PD Scorecard Studio
tagline: Build a classic PD scorecard on 30,000 public credit-card accounts: monotonic binning, WoE/IV feature selection, logistic regression, points scaling, calibration and Gini/KS validation. A Claude agent answers risk questions by calling validated scorecard tools (bad rates, IV tables, performance, score breakdowns) and explains results in validator-friendly language.

datasets.name: UCI_Credit_Card
limitations: Automated inspection: Snapshot inspected 2026-10-28; the source may change after this date.
Taiwan 2005 card portfolio, not Nordic; one observation window so no vintages or time-based PSI.
Zenodo record does not cite Yeh & Lien (2009) explicitly; matches the UCI 'Default of Credit Card Clients' description (30,000 rows, Apr-Sep 2005).
PAY_* codes include -2/-1/0 whose meaning is debated in the literature; treat as categorical bins.
SEX, MARRIAGE and AGE are protected or sensitive attributes; exclude SEX/MARRIAGE from the scorecard and only report them for fairness checks.

tools.name: bad_rate_by_segment
tools.description: Default rate and account count of default.payment.next.month grouped by a categorical driver (e.g. most recent repayment status PAY_0, EDUCATION).

tools.name: woe_iv_table
tools.description: Monotonic/quantile binning of one driver with per-bin counts, bad rate, WoE and total Information Value.

tools.name: scorecard_performance
tools.description: Fit (cached) WoE logistic scorecard on a seeded train split; return Gini, KS, AUC on train/test and a calibration table by score decile (predicted vs observed PD).

tools.name: score_breakdown
tools.description: Points contribution per characteristic for one account ID or a what-if input, with the resulting score and PD.

tools.name: filter_accounts
tools.description: Return accounts matching filters on repayment status and education, for drill-down.

example_questions: Which characteristics have the highest Information Value, and which would you drop?
What is the scorecard's Gini on the test set, and is it well calibrated by decile?
How does default rate change with the most recent repayment status PAY_0?
Why did account 1234 get its score? Which characteristics cost it the most points?
